verbatim_locators.note: Coverage of this pass: the whole main text of this Letter and the Methods read for one question (is the human postnatal SVZ/RMS compartment still active at the WOREE presentation age); figure captions only; supplementary unavailable on this route. The sample-size phrase '10 neurosurgical resections + 50 autopsied brains' quoted in the candidate was NOT located in the served body or abstract and is not carried. No WWOX datum exists in this paper; it measures the tissue, never the gene.

entries.proposition: Human SVZ immature-neuron density falls steeply in the first six months after birth (DCX+ cells, 25-fold), across 16 specimens aged 0-17 years.
entries.snippet: The emergence of the gap layer coincides with the decline in DCX(+) immature neurons (25-fold during the first 6 months; n=16, ages 0–17 years
entries.anchor: Main text (Letter; no section headings), SVZ cytoarchitecture paragraph

entries.proposition: Between 6 and 18 months the network of putative migratory neurons is depleted and the adult gap-layer structure appears; the compartment is still active at the ages at which WOREE presents.
entries.snippet: Progressively, between 6 to 18 months of age, the SVZ is depleted of this dense network of putative migratory neurons

entries.proposition: After 18 months proliferation and immature neurons are at adult trace levels.
entries.snippet: After 18 months, Ki67(+) proliferative activity and the number of DCX(+) immature neurons assume trace levels seen in adults

entries.proposition: The infant RMS is continuous at 1 day, 1 week, 1, 3 and 6 months in six autopsied brains.
entries.snippet: Using autopsied material (n=6) (ages 1 day; 1 week; 1, 3, and 6 months), serial sagittal and coronal reconstruction of the ventral forebrain revealed an uninterrupted column of cells

entries.proposition: A medial migratory stream to ventromedial prefrontal cortex is present at 4-6 months and absent at 8-18 months.
entries.snippet: This medial migratory stream (MMS) was observed in human specimens ages 4–6 months but not 8–18 months

entries.proposition: The MMS was looked for in mouse (P4-P20) and not found: a human-specific compartment no mouse window can model.
entries.snippet: We analyzed serial sections of mouse brains at P4, P8, P16 and P20 and did not detect a MMS
